snippet.title: Diamonds: The Greatest Scam in History | Rush
snippet.description:
A diamond is just carbon. The same element in your pencil. So how did one company convince the entire world to spend two months' salary on one?

In 1947, four words changed everything: "A Diamond is Forever." It wasn't a fact about geology. It was an ad campaign — arguably the most successful one ever created. Before it ran, barely 10% of American brides received a diamond ring. By 1990, that number hit 80%. And behind it all was one company that controlled 90% of the global supply.

This documentary traces the real story of diamonds — from their formation 3 billion years ago, 250 km below the Earth's surface, to the blood-soaked mines of Sierra Leone, to the polishing workshops of India where 9 out of 10 diamonds in the world are cut today.

snippet.title: Oil Crisis? The World's Energy Problem | Rush
snippet.description:
The Strait of Hormuz is blocked. Oil prices are surging. And for the third time in 50 years, the world is asking the same question: Why do we still depend on this?

In 1973, an oil embargo reshaped the global economy overnight. In 2022, Russia's gas cutoff sent Europe scrambling. Now in 2026, a single strait is holding 20% of the world's oil hostage — and history is repeating itself.

This documentary traces how energy built the modern world — and why oil's grip on it is starting to slip. We follow the money, the power, and the resources behind the biggest economic shift in human history: from fossil fuels that are running out to the technologies racing to replace them.

Solar went from $15/watt to $0.24. Hydrogen gigaprojects are being built across three continents. The lithium triangle in South America holds 75% of the world's battery resources — and everyone wants in. Meanwhile, hard-to-abate industries like steel and cement still can't function without carbon. So what happens to the CO₂? Turns out, it might be worth $6 trillion.
This isn't about ideology. It's about who controls the next era of energy — and who gets left behind.

snippet.title: The Crusaders: In the Name of Christ | Holy Wars | Classic Documentary
snippet.description:
The times were turbulent around 1100 AD, when West-Roman Christianity was spreading out in all directions. snippet.title: The Trial That Could Have Stopped Christianity ⚖️✝️
snippet.description:
Standing in the ruins of Ancient Corinth, it's hard to imagine that one of the most important moments in early Christian history happened right here. 🏛️

This is the Bema of Gallio, the place where St. Paul was brought before the Roman proconsul Gallio to answer accusations about his teachings. ⚖️

The outcome of that trial had enormous consequences. Rather than stopping the spread of Christianity, it allowed the new faith to continue growing throughout the Roman Empire. ✝️

Today, visitors can stand in the very place where faith, politics, and history collided nearly 2,000 years ago.
